questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: Why people love biscuits
Lying: why we do it and how to spot it
How to win a lying competition
Why lawyers are good at their jobs
questions.why: Rob says the topic is lying and how to detect it.

questions.q: Why does Rob say the programme is about biscuits?
options: It was the original topic
He was hungry
To demonstrate a lie at the start
Sam asked him to
questions.why: He says he was lying 'simply to demonstrate our topic'.

questions.q: How did Sam know Rob was lying?
options: From the smirk on his face
His face turned red
He paused before answering
He shuffled his feet
questions.why: Sam says, 'I could tell by the smirk on your face.'

questions.q: According to Sophie Scott, why is normal conversation often not completely truthful?
options: Most people secretly want to cheat others for money
People often forget what they really think about things
People are afraid of being punished for being honest
We stay polite by not saying exactly what we think
questions.why: She says cooperation is at the heart of social interaction, making conversation polite and not truthful.

questions.q: What is the difference between deceiving someone and telling a white lie, according to the presenters?
options: A white lie is not meant to gain an advantage
A white lie is always bigger
Deceiving is only done with actions, not words
There is no real difference
questions.why: Sam says white lies avoid upsetting someone and aren't intended to give you an advantage.

questions.q: According to Richard Wiseman, which is a sign someone might be lying?
options: They talk much more than usual
They answer very quickly
They take longer to start answering
They use 'I' and 'my' a lot
questions.why: He says liars tend to have a longer response latency before answering.

questions.q: What else does Richard Wiseman say about the words liars use?
options: They use many more emotional words than usual
They repeat the question before they answer it
They speak much more formally and slowly
Words like 'me', 'my' and 'I' tend to disappear
questions.why: He says there's emotional distance, so 'me', 'my', 'I' tend to drop away.

questions.q: What does Sam think of Rob's summary of Richard Wiseman's advice?
options: It is completely correct and clear
It is only partly right; there's more to it
It is a lie that Rob made up himself
It is far too long and hard to follow
questions.why: Sam says 'Sort of' and adds that there's probably more to it than that.
